hypothesis: Question-only decomposition improves complete evidence and answer coverage under the same final context budget.

arms.a: Current vector_context retrieval with original query
arms.b: Original query plus at most four question-only subqueries; original first result then subquery round-robin and original list; deduplicate exact spans and body within notice scope

evaluation.retrieval: Each predeclared answer item requires its source-scoped phrase group across the union of actual supplied bodies. Report item and complete-question coverage as automatic proxies, not semantic accuracy.
evaluation.generation: Assistant compares all output facts and completeness against fixed rubric and supplied citations for both arms. Partial/abstained answer on answerable question is not full success. Separate message facts are included. Human approval is absent.
evaluation.planner: Review loss or invention of constraints separately; no evidence or labels in model input.
evaluation.cost: Report planning plus both arms' generation SDK usage, per-stage latency and errors. Final evidence cap is equal; total compute budget is not equal.
evaluation.decision: Retain as experimental unless heldout complete evidence and full-answer count improve, simple and behavior cases do not regress, and no new unsupported answer claims appear. Small sample is not a production gate.
evaluation.no_posthoc_tuning: No algorithm/prompt/label tuning after observing experiment outcomes; any subsequent tuning requires a fresh heldout set. Preserve proxy errors and add semantic review separately.

limitations: Single stochastic generation sample per arm
Round-robin represents candidate lists, not verified answer-item coverage
Question decomposition can omit constraints or introduce semantic drift even after structural validation
